Welcome to Halfway Houses
At Halfway Houses Primary School we celebrate uniqueness and difference and ensure that everyone has the freedom to lead their own learning. We hope to provide creative, diverse and inspirational opportunities and environments in which every member of our community can enjoy learning and feel valued.

We are part ofThe Island Learning Trust
We are committed to creating a learning community in which children are perseverant, resilient risk takers who take responsibility for their learning and develop their critical creative and social abilities fully.
We believe that children learn best when learning is: exciting, challenging, creative, collaborative, practical, reflective and meaningful. Learning should inspire children to ask questions and to wonder. It should provide them with memorable experiences.

pageCache.text:
Reading Ambassadors
Our Wonderful Reading Ambassadors for the Year 2024-25
We have 24 pupil Reading Ambassadors who help promote reading for pleasure throughout our school. They all carry out a duty in the school library once a week, where they; help younger pupils choose suitable books, encourage our pupils to discover new books and authors to enjoy and assist the librarians with organising the library.
Our Reading Recommendations
Keep an eye on this page for our chosen book recommendations...
Our Reading Ambassadors will be leaving special book marks inside the books they've read that they would like to recommend to others to read too.
Keep your eyes peeled when you're next in the school library! You might discover a new favourite...

pageCache.text:
Consultation: Proposed Nursery Provision at Halfway Houses Primary School
News and Events
Consultation: Proposed Nursery Provision at Halfway Houses Primary School
Consultation period 6 weeks. Opens 14th January and closes 25th February
Purpose of Consultation
We are seeking your views on our proposal to establish a term time only, school-based nursery for 2–4-year-olds at Halfway Houses Primary School to open September 2026. This initiative responds to a growing local need for high-quality early years provision and aligns with our vision of ensuring every child fulfils their potential with confidence.
Location: Two existing classrooms will be converted into a dedicated nursery space.
Local Need: Demand for nursery places is increasing due to new housing developments and changes in childcare funding.
Benefits for Children:
Benefits for Families:
The Island Learning Trust would welcome any comments that you would like to raise related to this proposal via email to hhoffice@tiltrust.org
Large and flexible internal learning space
Access to large Forest School Area
Early identification of learning needs.
Strong transition into primary education.
Access to Forest School and outdoor learning.
Opportunities for parental engagement and workshops.
